key_insight: BenchX shows that cancer-detection AI can look strong on average while performing much worse in specific patient groups, tumor sizes, and imaging protocols.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark highlights the need to test medical AI across demographic and scan-protocol subgroups so clinicians and developers can better identify hidden performance gaps before deployment.
method: Built an open benchmark of 85,355 CT scans
Evaluated 12 tumor-detection AI models across tumor size, location, patient subgroup, and imaging protocol
Used LLMs to extract and organize subgroup information from clinical data
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic evaluation of 12 models on 85,355 CT scans, revealing poor performance in rare or underrepresented subgroups.
watch_item: Subgroup findings depend on the quality of extracted clinical labels and may not fully solve the problem of sparse data for rare populations.
paper_title: BenchX: Benchmarking AI Models for Cancer Detection and Localization with Demographic and Protocol Biases
